lead.hed: Two Space Force officers finished the Army's jungle course in Panama
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Friday: Maj. Alyson Gleason and Capt. Stephen Brown became the first U.S. Space Force members to complete the Jungle Operations Training Course-Panama, graduating Sept. 25 at Aeronaval Base Cristóbal Colón. The 18-day course put them with Army soldiers and Panamanian partners. First class of Guardians through the course, not a change in Space Force mission.
lead.image_credit: Pfc. Carolyn Dodge · DVIDS 9967484 · Public domain · Graduates of Jungle Operations Training Course-Panama Class 26-007 at Aeronaval Base Cristóbal Colón, Panama, Sept. 25, 2026.

political.hed: Treating a child as the opposite sex is not the legal definition of abuse, a report argues
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: institutions built to protect children are under scrutiny after parents lost custody for refusing to treat a gender-confused child as the opposite sex. The report says those cases rest on an ideological premise, not the legal definition of abuse. Report, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

political.hed: NORAD will enforce weekend flight restrictions over Knoxville and Chicago
political.insight: DVIDS, posted Friday from Tyndall Air Force Base: NORAD will enforce FAA VIP temporary flight restrictions this weekend, Sept. 26–27, over Knoxville, Tennessee, and Chicago. Pilots are told to check notices before each flight. Enforcement notice, not a new air-defense mission.

political.hed: A witness told Congress the cause is a pretext and the aim is disruption
political.insight: Heritage, Thursday: testimony before a House panel said a red-green alliance of Marxist and Islamist groups works with foreign governments to disrupt everyday life and the democratic process, using whatever cause is at hand. Testimony summary, not a floor vote. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: An appeals court upheld the Pentagon's blacklist of Anthropic
tech.insight: Defense News, Friday, citing Reuters: a 2-1 decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington upheld the Pentagon's March designation of Anthropic as a national security supply-chain risk after the company refused to allow its products for autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. Court ruling, not a new contract award.

tech.hed: A Friday essay recovers a Colombian reactionary as a defender of a free society
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: the piece says Nicolás Gómez Dávila, the Bogotá aphorist called the Nietzsche of the Andes, distrusted social engineers who try to remake societies and reshape persons. Essay, not a statute.

culture.hed: Marijuana law should teach, not only shrink the black market, an essay argues
culture.insight: American Reformer, Thursday: the essay says many Christians accepted legalization as a way to shrink black markets, then argues that classical law also forms citizens. It notes a Justice Department move of FDA-approved marijuana products from Schedule I to Schedule III. Argument, not a new statute. Not a reprint of Friday's book review.

culture.hed: An essay traces the friendship behind U.S. religious-freedom law
culture.insight: Public Discourse, Friday: Thomas Farr writes that Frank Wolf and Chris Smith met in Bucharest in 1985 and later wrote the 1998 International Religious Freedom Act and the 2016 Frank Wolf revision. The Religious Freedom Institute will give them this year's Defender of Religious Freedom award. Essay, not a new statute.
